raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Capture the rest of the DFlash/DSpark context preparation in the draft's FULL CUDA graph, ahead of the query forward: combine the target's auxiliary hidden states, publish the LiLiCorr context anchor, then precompute the context K/V. #57632 captured only the last step; the first two still ran eagerly before every replay.

- The target's auxiliary states are staged into a fixed-address buffer before replay. The buffer is allocated at capture, only when the draft captures FULL graphs, so memory profiling accounts for it and an eager fallback does not hold it.
- LiLiCorr owns a fixed-address copy of the rejection counts its anchor reads; DFlash, DFlash2 and DSpark skip that copy.
- Context rows beyond the graph's capacity, and non-FULL paths, still run eagerly.
- The eager warmup before capture is preserved, including the Kimi-K3 cache-pointer refresh from #58814.

Applies to the shared DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark and LiLiCorr path. Open-PR searches for `dflash graph context`, `combine_hidden_states` and `57632 in:body` found no PR capturing this prologue; #50658 instead moves Kimi-K3 auxiliary projection before the SP all-gather.

## Test Plan

- E2E decode ITL: TP4 + DSpark serving benchmark, base vs PR vs base again on one node.
- Accuracy and acceptance: full GSM8K with DSpark on TP4 (PR) and DEP4 (base and PR).
- Microbenchmark of the context prologue alone.
- Unit tests, including a new CUDA graph test of the captured context step.

## Test Result

### E2E decode ITL (TP4, DSpark)

| Workload | Base | PR | Base (rerun) | PR vs base |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 in / 1024 out, c=1 | 5.66 | **5.55** | 5.91 | −2% / −6% |
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c=1 | 5.68 | **5.54** | 5.91 | −2% / −6% |
| 128 in / 1024 out, c=8 | 10.84 | 10.81 | 10.81 | no measurable difference |
| 128 in / 1024 out, c=64 | 26.61 | 26.59 | 26.62 | no measurable difference |

Median ITL p50 (ms) of 3 repeats. Every PR run at c=1 (5.53–5.59 ms) is below every base run (5.55–5.97 ms). Batch-1 decode is host-bound, and host CPU time varies more across runs than GPU time: the base's c=1 ITL moved by about 5% between its two runs, so the gain is quoted against each (−2% vs the run before the PR, −6% vs the run after). At c=8 and c=64 the step is GPU-bound and the host saving is not visible.

<details>
<summary>Setup</summary>

- 4× GB200, one node and one job: base (`8fb16ea5a6`) → PR (`ff8da0a4d8`) → base again, from the same source path and venv. The follow-up commits `9286fbea34` and `32836b7d4e` only move the staging allocation, restrict the rejection-count copy to LiLiCorr and simplify the test; they do not change the DSpark path measured here.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`), TP4 (no expert parallel), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, fp8 KV cache, prefix caching off, FlashInfer autotune off, NUMA bind.
- DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and synthetic acceptance length 6.0, so every draft is accepted (100% from `/metrics` in every run).
- Random dataset with range ratio 0, `--ignore-eos`, 4× concurrency prompts (at least 8), unique seed per workload, concurrency and repeat. Each side is warmed up on every workload first; no timed run had runtime JIT warnings or new DeepGEMM cache entries. No probes or profilers.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 131072 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":6.0}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' --numa-bind --numa-bind-nodes 0 0 1 1

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-input-len <128|8192> --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <1|8|64>
```

</details>

### Accuracy and acceptance (GSM8K, DSpark)

| Topology | Side | GSM8K strict | Acceptance length, incl. bonus | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| TP4, fixed verification | PR | 93.03% | 3.449 | 0.794 / 0.649 / 0.459 / 0.335 / 0.213 |
| DEP4, MegaMoE, adaptive verification | base | 92.57% | 3.365 | 0.792 / 0.641 / 0.441 / 0.310 / 0.181 |
| DEP4, MegaMoE, adaptive verification | PR, run 1 | 92.34% | 3.367 | 0.792 / 0.642 / 0.440 / 0.310 / 0.183 |
| DEP4, MegaMoE, adaptive verification | PR, run 2 | 92.49% | 3.330 | 0.793 / 0.635 / 0.430 / 0.299 / 0.173 |

Full GSM8K (1319 problems, 5-shot completions, greedy, 1024 output tokens, concurrency 32, strict match), one pass per server, 0 request errors, acceptance from the engine's `/metrics` counters. PR is `ff8da0a4d8`; the follow-up commits do not change the DSpark path.

- DEP4: base (`8fb16ea5a6`) and PR on the same node and source path. Acceptance matches within 1% and the per-position curves overlap; GSM8K differs by at most 3/1319, inside run-to-run noise (two DEP4 baseline repeats in #57632 differed by 18/1319).
- TP4: PR side only. It matches #57632's TP4 reference (3.471 / 93.03%).

<details>
<summary>GSM8K server configuration</summary>

Same flags as #57632's GSM8K runs, plus FlashInfer autotune off:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  <TP4: --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}'> \
  <DEP4: --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}'> \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":<false on TP4, true on DEP4>}'
```

</details>

### Microbenchmark (context prologue only)

Single GB200, real MXFP8 `main_proj` weights (`15360 → 5120`) and RMSNorm, simulated BF16 auxiliary states from three target layers, 5 speculative tokens (6 context rows per request). CPU is submission wall time, median of three runs of 200 alternating samples; GPU is FlashInfer CUPTI with cold L2 on the captured prologue.

| requests | context rows | CPU before (µs) | CPU after (µs) | GPU before / after (µs) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6 | 392.6 | 48.8 | 34.4 / 36.3 |
| 8 | 48 | 396.1 | 49.9 | 46.8 / 49.5 |
| 32 | 192 | 386.7 | 49.4 | 51.2 / 52.7 |
| 128 | 768 | 327.4 | 48.3 | 88.6 / 89.9 |
| 256 | 1536 | 331.9 | 50.0 | 154.3 / 156.0 |
| 1, prefill | 8192 | 350.0 | 386.7 | 791.3 / 794.9 |

Decode saves 0.28–0.35 ms of CPU per step. A prefill pays ~37 µs more because the projection is split between the graph prefix and the eager tail. Context outputs matched exactly for three fresh inputs per shape; padded GEMM shapes need not be bitwise identical in general.

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py
```

92 passed. `test_captured_context_anchor_rereads_fixed_inputs` captures the context step and checks that replays re-read the anchor's fixed-address inputs, ignore a padded request's stale rejection count, and anchor on a row stored eagerly past the graph's capacity.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used. Codex assisted with review and the microbenchmark; Claude Code with the E2E and GSM8K runs, the follow-up commit and this description. All changes were reviewed by the author.

+        _precompute_context_kv=lambda start, end: None,
